Every time you paste a URL or drop a file into my OpenCode CLI, a decision engine wakes up. It classifies the input, pulls together the right skills, scripts, and phases, then executes a multi-step pipeline — all from a single YAML file. Here's how it works.

## The Problem

I was tired of writing one-off scripts for every content pipeline. YouTube videos needed transcript extraction and blog formatting. GitHub repos needed analysis. News articles needed summarisation. Each had its own workflow, its own error handling, its own set of chained tools.

What I wanted was a single declarative registry that said: "when you see input type X, offer these flows, and execute them using these phases."

## The Architecture

The system has four layers:

1. **Detection** — pattern-matches the input against 6 types
2. **Classification** — loads the flow registry from `flows.yaml`
3. **Phase Engine** — orchestrates execution with shared-phase deduplication
4. **Presentation** — menu system via `build_menu.py` (mobile: 4 items, desktop: 8)

## Six Input Types, Forty Flows

The `flows.yaml` defines detection patterns and available flows for each input type:

| Input | Detection | Flows |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **YouTube** | `youtube.com/watch`, `youtu.be/`, `youtube.com/shorts/` | 11 — blog posts (narrative/tutorial/analysis), video+blog, audio+blog, streaming, eRAG, project context, VKE ingestion, env review |
| **GitHub** | `github.com/{owner}/{repo}` | 7 — VKE, env review, blog post, env analysis, setup/deploy, find alternatives, deep analysis |
| **Web URL** | Any `https://` link | 8 — VKE, env review, summarise, publish blog, blog with commentary, add to project, eRAG, cross-reference |
| **File** | `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.csv`, `.xlsx`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.txt`, `.md` | 7 — VKE, summarise, compare, eRAG, extract data, metadata+telos, remind |
| **News** | `bbc.co.uk`, `theguardian.com`, `reuters.com`, `nytimes.com` | 4 — summarise, blog post, eRAG, cross-reference |
| **Shop** | UK supermarket domains | 3 — summarise, compare prices, eRAG |

## How the Phase Engine Works

Each flow defines a sequence of phases with standardised emojis:

| Phase | Emoji | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Extract | 🟡 | Pull content (transcript, file text, web scrape) |
| Download | 🟠 | MeTube video/audio download |
| Validate | 🟡 | Quality gate the extracted content |
| Analyse | 🟢 | Run analysis, comparison, cross-reference |
| Publish | 🔵 | Push to blog via Directus API |
| Notify | 🟣 | Send Telegram notification |
| Report | 🟣 | Generate integration report |

The phase engine (`phase_engine.py`) does something clever: **shared phase deduplication**. When you select multiple flows that share phases (e.g., both "stream video" and "blog post" need the extract phase), the engine runs the shared phase once and passes the result to all dependent flows.

## YouTube: The Most Complex Pipeline

YouTube gets the richest treatment because it has the most downstream flows:

1. **Background extraction** starts immediately — before the user even picks a flow, `extract-youtube-transcript.sh` is already running inside the MeTube container
2. **Menu appears** with 11 flow options (single-select since blog types are mutually exclusive)
3. **Phase engine executes** the selected flow, potentially combining transcript extraction with MeTube download in parallel
4. **Blog posts** get an embedded HTML5 player if streaming was also selected

The transcript extraction script tries three methods in sequence: `yt-dlp --write-auto-sub`, then `--write-sub`, then Python regex on the description for reference links.

## The Menu System

The ingestion router integrates with the menu-factory system. When a URL is detected:

1. `build_menu.py` reads the session mode (mobile/desktop) from `.session_mode.json`
2. It loads global-config.json for max items and suffix options
3. It appends mandatory options (env integration review) from `skill-mandatory-ingestion-router.json`
4. It truncates to fit (mobile: 4 items, desktop: 8)
5. It records present/select signals for the menu optimizer

The menu is never hardcoded — it's derived at runtime from the flow registry plus global configuration.

## The Same Flows in the Dashboard

The standalone chat dashboard at `ubuntu4:8058` shares the same flow registry. The FastAPI backend serves `GET /ingest/flows` directly from `flows.yaml`, and the React frontend's `IngestionRouter.tsx` component classifies URLs client-side, then shows animated flow buttons with stagger-in effects.

This means whether you paste a YouTube URL into the CLI or the web dashboard, you get the same pipeline options — the same blog post types, the same eRAG ingestion, the same streaming flows.

## Blog Post Types: Three Flavours

For YouTube and other content sources, blog posts come in three types, each with its own Diataxis category and structure:

| Type | Words | Voice | Structure |
|------|-------|-------|-----------|
| **Narrative** | 900-1200 | First-person | Problem → trap → solution → evidence → lessons |
| **Tutorial** | 1400-1800 | Second-person | Mental model → numbered steps → validation → mistakes → generalisation |
| **Analysis** | 1200-1500 | Analytical | Question → evidence → counter-arguments → conclusion → implications |

These are flattened into separate flow IDs (`blog-post-narrative`, `blog-post-tutorial`, `blog-post-analysis`) so there's no sub-menu — the user picks the type directly.

## VKE: The Knowledge Engine Integration

Every input type includes a VKE (Verified Knowledge Engine) ingestion flow that follows the Karpathy pattern:

`raw/` → compile → lint → `wiki/`

Raw input lands in `~/.config/opencode/raw/`, gets processed by `brainplane_cleaner.py`, and if it passes quality gates, graduates to `~/.config/opencode/wiki/` as structured knowledge. This means every YouTube video, every GitHub repo, every article can become permanent searchable knowledge.

## What I Learned Building This

The biggest insight was making flows declarative rather than procedural. Instead of writing a Python function for each pipeline, I define them in YAML with standardised phases. The phase engine handles orchestration, deduplication, and error reporting. Adding a new flow is just adding a YAML entry — no code changes.

The second insight was the menu-factory integration. By deriving menus at runtime instead of hardcoding them, the system adapts to session mode, usage patterns (via signal tracking), and mandatory option injection — all without touching the flow definitions.

The third was parallel extraction. For YouTube, starting transcript extraction before the user picks a flow saves 10-30 seconds. By the time they decide, the content is already available.
